claims.explanation: Fluspirilene is a diphenylbutylpiperidine antipsychotic that acts as a potent antagonist of voltage-gated calcium channels and dopamine receptors, and it also inhibits CDK2. Its selective anticancer activity likely depends on cancer cells relying on calcium signaling for survival and on CDK2 activity for proliferation. Thus, tumors with high expression of calcium channel subunits (e.g., CACNA1C) or high CDK2 activity would be more sensitive, while those with low expression or high efflux capacity would be protected.

features.basis: Fluspirilene blocks L-type calcium channels; high expression increases dependence on calcium signaling for survival.
Fluspirilene identified as a CDK2 inhibitor; high CDK2 activity predicts sensitivity to CDK2 inhibition.
Fluspirilene is a dopamine D2 receptor antagonist; high DRD2 expression may mediate antiproliferative effects.
Fluspirilene induces autophagy by preventing calpain1-mediated cleavage of ATG5; high full-length ATG5 may protect cells by promoting survival autophagy.
Fluspirilene inhibits calpain1, leading to increased full-length ATG5 and autophagy; high calpain1 may indicate dependence on this pathway.
Fluspirilene blocks N-type calcium channels; high expression may increase sensitivity.
Fluspirilene blocks P/Q-type calcium channels; high expression may increase sensitivity.
Fluspirilene blocks R-type calcium channels; high expression may increase sensitivity.
Fluspirilene is metabolized by CYP3A4; high expression may reduce drug exposure and protect cells.
Fluspirilene metabolism may involve CYP2D6; high expression could reduce drug efficacy.
Fluspirilene induces apoptosis via p53; loss-of-function mutations may confer resistance.
Fluspirilene suppresses STAT3 signaling; high STAT3 activity may indicate dependence and sensitivity.
